messages:
Miguel (support): Hey team, ACME on Dedicated flagged negative tokens/sec in the Console for their streaming routes and their monthly bill shows a small credit. Customer is alarmed. Screenshot + tenant id: https://rlwd.in/snap/acme-neg.png. Happened starting ~2026-03-15 10:23 UTC. Can we triage? :warning:

Amy (console): Ugh. I see a sequence of windows that go 120, 98, -15, -8, 130 in the tokens/sec chart for model-route prod/stream-1. Chart tooltip shows window size 60s.

Raj (eng-oncall): Thanks — assigning to eng-oncall. Miguel: do you have the raw rollup rows (window_start + partition counters) for that tenant/time? Also, did ACME change any routing or retry logic?

Miguel (support): I grabbed the raw counters from the customer-facing metrics API: attached CSV and a short query I ran. No app changes reported. CSV excerpt:

```
window_start,partition,counter
2026-03-15T10:20:00Z,0,102340
2026-03-15T10:21:00Z,0,102400
2026-03-15T10:22:00Z,0,102460
2026-03-15T10:23:00Z,0,102440   <-- counter decreased
2026-03-15T10:24:00Z,0,102432
```

Miguel (support): The decrease in the raw counter is what produced negative delta for that partition, which then shows up in tokens/sec after aggregation.

Raj (eng-oncall): Good repro. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) a partition consumer replay/reset wrote older counters (offset regression), 2) compaction/ingestion bug where counters from different epochs mixed. Any deploys touching the rollup writer or consumer around 10:15-10:30 UTC?

Amy (console): I just checked deploy history — there was a small change to rollup alignment flags rolled out at 10:10 UTC (PR #1423) that flips how we align windows when partitions are rebalanced. Could explain mis-ordered writes.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-42 — streaming rollup negative-delta spikes (assigned to eng-oncall).

Raj (eng-oncall): Steps I'm taking now:
- grabbing consumer-group offsets and commit history for the tenant partitions from Kafka (will paste)
- running a query to compute per-partition delta and show how negative deltas correlate with partition movement

(Quick debug query I ran against internal metrics store:)
```
SELECT window_start,
  partition,
  counter,
  counter - LAG(counter) OVER (PARTITION BY partition ORDER BY window_start) AS delta
FROM streaming_counters
WHERE tenant_id = 'acme' AND window_start >= '2026-03-15T10:15:00Z'
ORDER BY window_start, partition
```
Sample output shows negative delta at 10:23 for partition 0 and 2.

Amy (console): If the consumer replayed older offsets, the counters could go backwards. For billing we rely on deltas — negative values produce credits or clamp to zero depending on downstream. Looks like the Console aggregator currently shows raw sum (including negatives) which is why charts dip below zero.

Miguel (support): Customer timeline: they saw the anomaly for ~2 minutes, then everything resumed. They've asked for an explanation and to confirm billing won't be impacted.

Raj (eng-oncall): Immediate mitigation options (short list):
- Patch rollup aggregators to clamp per-partition delta to >=0 before summing (hotfix) — low risk, will make charts/billing non-negative.
- Recompute affected windows from raw event log for the tenant and regenerate rollups (backfill) — accurate, longer run.

Amy (console): I can push a UI-side clamp so charts don't show negatives within 15m, but that hides underlying data — prefer server-side clamp + backfill.

Raj (eng-oncall): Agreed. Plan: 1) hotfix aggregator to apply max(delta,0) at sum-time and release to prod (target: +30m). 2) start a backfill job for 10:15–10:30 UTC for tenant acme (recompute from event log) and validate token sums (ticket: BACKFILL-874). 3) postmortem and add monotonicity check alert.

Amy (console): I'll prepare a customer-facing note template explaining root cause and remediation. Miguel can you share the invoice line impacted once backfill finishes so billing can correct?

Miguel (support): Will do. Also raising with billing team now — they asked for the exact windows and affected amount estimate.

Raj (eng-oncall): Progress update: found consumer rejoin at 10:22:31 UTC with offset rewind of ~2 minutes on partition 0 and 2. That aligns perfectly. Root cause appears to be the deploy at 10:10 that changed alignment + an unhandled consumer rebalance path that wrote counters with non-monotonic timestamps.

Raj (eng-oncall): Hotfix PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollups/pull/1489 — adds safety clamp and a histogram metric for negative-delta-count. Rolling to prod canary now.

sre-bot: Deploy canary started for rollups v1.8.3-canary by raj — 3 nodes.

Amy (console): Canary looks clean on canary tenants. No further negative points in the sample tenant graphs. If canary stays green for 10 minutes, promote.

Miguel (support): I sent the customer a short note: we detected non-monotonic counter writes during a brief consumer rebalance, pushed a safety fix, and are backfilling to correct metrics and billing. They've acknowledged and asked for ETA on backfill.

Raj (eng-oncall): Backfill kicked off (BACKFILL-874 job id bf-2026-0315-22). Estimated completion 45min for this tenant range. When done we'll validate sums and generate corrected rollup blobs and a billing adjustment if needed.

Amy (console): Action items and owners:
- Raj: complete hotfix rollout and monitor negative-delta metric (in progress).
- Raj: finish backfill and post results in thread (bf job id above).
- Miguel: coordinate billing + customer comms; capture affected invoice lines.
- Amy: prepare FAQ for Console (why could I see negative tokens/sec).

Raj (eng-oncall): Long-term fix proposals: add monotonicity enforcement in the ingestion pipeline (reject/backpressure non-monotonic writes), add end-to-end tests for consumer rebalances, and revert the alignment change until we prove safety. I'll open RFC.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-42 status -> mitigated (hotfix applied); monitoring for regressions.

Miguel (support): Customer updated: they appreciate the quick response. Will wait for final confirmation before billing adjustment. Thanks everyone. :pray:
